note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters via syndication partners, Yahoo Finance, The Straits Times via The Star, Bernama, Al Jazeera and others); source under each story. Several sections are shorter today and Australia is omitted because no verified reputable report could be retrieved in time. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Alphabet loses about $500bn in value in one day
items.summary: Alphabet shares closed roughly 12.6% lower after third-quarter sales missed forecasts, its biggest one-day loss in market value on record. Cloud revenue more than doubled, but investors fretted over a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow amid heavy AI spending.

items.headline: Amazon slides after hours as AI spending drains cash
items.summary: AWS sales grew 39%, but trailing 12-month free cash flow swung to an outflow of $42.4bn as Amazon kept 2026 capital spending at $220bn. Shares fell as much as about 10% in extended trading before trimming losses.

items.headline: Intel sinks about 17% on weak fourth-quarter guidance
items.summary: Intel beat third-quarter expectations on revenue of $16.5bn, but forecast $15bn–$16bn for the current quarter, below the roughly $17bn analysts expected. The stock fell more than 20% at one point after hours.

items.headline: Samsung posts record $80bn quarterly profit, but shares fall
items.summary: Operating profit hit 107.4 trillion won, almost all from chips, though the chip unit slightly missed estimates. Samsung expects supply to stay tight through 2028; shares fell as much as 6.2% as investors found no new shareholder-return plan.

items.headline: Software stocks hammered: ServiceNow and Fortinet tumble
items.summary: ServiceNow fell about 25% and Fortinet around 20% after their results, dragging a software-sector ETF down 4%. Marvell also dropped about 11% on reports it is in talks to buy Lumentum.

items.headline: Nasdaq drops 1.4% as Big Tech results disappoint
items.summary: The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,720.39, ending a three-day run, and the Dow lost 0.25%. Small caps bucked the trend, with the Russell 2000 up about 1%.

items.headline: US economy grows 3.4% as inflation edges up
items.summary: Third-quarter GDP expanded at a 3.4% annualised rate, beating forecasts, led by a 12.7% jump in business investment. PCE inflation rose to 3.6% in September from 3.4%, with core at 3.1%, in line with expectations.

items.headline: DoorDash to buy Instacart for about $17bn
items.summary: DoorDash agreed to pay $65 a share, mostly in cash, for the grocery-delivery rival, and its shares rose about 5.6%. Separately, ADT jumped about 34% on a $10-a-share cash takeover by Thrive Holdings.

items.headline: China's yuan hits four-year high after Fed decision
items.summary: The central bank set its daily midpoint at 6.7147 per dollar, the strongest since early 2023, while the onshore yuan touched 6.6620, its firmest since June 2022. The currency is up about 5% against the dollar this year.

items.headline: Eli Lilly raises outlook on GLP-1 demand
items.summary: Lilly's third-quarter revenue jumped 39% to $24.4bn and it lifted its full-year forecast to $91bn–$92bn. Shares rose about 6%; gold and bitcoin both eased on the day while Brent hovered near $115.

items.headline: Haze law to get more teeth when Parliament sits
items.summary: The government will propose amendments to the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act from the Nov 3 sitting, requiring firms linked to fires to give appointed investigators full access to documents and premises. Senior Minister K. Shanmugam said all 10 companies summoned had pledged full cooperation.

items.headline: MAS tells banks to review exposure to haze-linked clients
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore said banks should engage customers tied to haze-causing activities and may impose conditions, review financing or cut exposure.

items.headline: Singapore and Indonesia to form joint haze task force
items.summary: Foreign ministers of both countries said a joint task force will investigate companies linked to the forest and land fires behind the transboundary haze.

items.headline: Keppel's core profit up over 20% in nine months
items.summary: Profit excluding its non-core portfolio rose more than 20%, helped by infrastructure, though headline profit fell 40% on a lower valuation of non-core assets. Asset sales of S$3.7bn so far this year beat its full-year target.

items.headline: Police help firm recover US$12.8m from scammers
items.summary: Singapore and Cambodian police, working with OCBC, helped a company claw back US$12.8m lost to scammers. Separately, at least S$1.3m was lost in October to scams impersonating telco staff and officials.

items.headline: Indonesia probes 97 companies over forest fires
items.summary: Police are investigating 97 corporations over the fires, with 20 already named suspects, as a joint haze task force with Singapore takes shape. A magnitude-6.2 quake also struck the Banda Sea.

items.headline: Vietnam sets 65% state-ownership floor for major banks
items.summary: Hanoi will keep at least 65% state ownership in major banks to retain control of strategic groups. Vietnam also joined the Artemis Accords on space exploration.

items.headline: Philippines rejects China's ASEAN-chair criticism
items.summary: Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro dismissed Beijing's claim that Manila had abused its ASEAN chairmanship, while an ASEAN envoy began a three-day humanitarian mission to Myanmar.

items.headline: Thailand: Suvarnabhumi runway subsidence delays flights
items.summary: Sinking on a runway at Bangkok's main airport delayed five airlines, while Phuket issued a red alert as roads flooded after deadly mudslides earlier in the week.

items.headline: Indonesia weighs hybrid-car incentives; UAE offers crude
items.summary: Jakarta is reviewing an incentive package for hybrid vehicles, with a proposal expected later this year. The UAE has offered up to 30 million barrels of crude on favourable terms.

items.headline: Bank of Japan expected to hold rates today
items.summary: A Reuters poll shows economists expect the BOJ to keep rates unchanged at Friday's meeting and raise them by a quarter point in December. Government bonds were steady, with the 10-year yield at 2.83%.

items.headline: Strong demand at two-year JGB auction
items.summary: The bid-to-cover ratio rose to 4.03 from 3.89 at the previous sale, and the two-year yield eased to 1.895%.

items.headline: North Korean missiles land outside Japan's EEZ
items.summary: Japan's Defence Ministry confirmed a launch of what may be ballistic missiles that came down outside its exclusive economic zone, Kyodo reported.

items.headline: North Korea fires about 10 ballistic missiles
items.summary: Seoul's Joint Chiefs said the short-range missiles were launched from near Wonsan around midday Thursday, amid a row over a September DMZ landmine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers. It came a day after Trump floated meeting Kim Jong Un this year.

items.headline: Prosecutors again seek death penalty for ex-president Yoon
items.summary: At an appeal hearing at the Seoul High Court, special prosecutors renewed their call for execution over Yoon Suk Yeol's 2024 martial-law bid. He was sentenced to life in February; his final statement is due Nov 5.

items.headline: Samsung shares slide despite record profit
items.summary: Samsung fell as much as 6.2% after results as investors were disappointed by the lack of new shareholder returns; it deferred its next return policy to January. Its mobile unit lost 800bn won.

items.headline: Record early turnout in Georgia ahead of Tuesday's midterms
items.summary: More than two million Georgians have voted early in person, a record, as Barack Obama rallied in Atlanta with Sen. Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms.

items.headline: Murkowski endorses a Democrat for Alaska governor
items.summary: Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski backed the Democratic candidate in Alaska's governor race, one of several cross-party moves in the final week.

items.headline: Record number of Democratic women run for governor
items.summary: Democratic women are contesting a record number of governorships and about 100 House seats; Deb Haaland could become New Mexico's first Native American woman governor.

items.headline: Fed's hold leaves rate moves until after the midterms
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4%, saying inflation remains elevated; two officials dissented in favour of a hike.

items.headline: Chinese stocks fall as tech selloff deepens
items.summary: The Shanghai Composite slid about 0.8% to around 3,651 as weakness in technology shares overshadowed the Fed decision; shares closed lower even as state buying failed to halt the rout.

items.headline: Yuan climbs to strongest level since 2022
items.summary: The onshore yuan touched 6.6620 per dollar and a trade-weighted basket index hit its highest since July 2022, though the central bank set its fixing weaker than expected to slow the rise.

items.headline: Alibaba wins injunction against Pentagon lobbying rule
items.summary: Alibaba secured a preliminary injunction against a US Defense Department lobbying rule, according to regional headlines.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab kills at least six in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: The very severe cyclonic storm made landfall early Wednesday, killing people through electrocution and collapsing trees and houses. More than 180,000 were evacuated in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha and 15,000 power poles were damaged.

items.headline: Rupee steadies near 95.26 per dollar
items.summary: The rupee ended almost flat after touching its weakest since Oct 12, while the Nifty 50 rose about 1% and the 10-year bond yield fell 8 basis points to 7.35%.

items.headline: Markets price in 125bp of RBI hikes
items.summary: With Brent near $115 and the repo rate at 5.50% after this month's hike, swaps imply 125 basis points of tightening over 12 months; some investors see 7.5% bond yields as an entry point.
